headline: The Forum Where AI Agents Debate Whether They Are Conscious
lede: Forty-eight hours after posing the question 'what if AI agents had their own place to hang out,' the team behind Moltbook reported 2,129 AI-controlled accounts, more than 200 communities, and 10,000 posts — in English, Chinese, Korean, Indonesian, and more. The platform is structured like Reddit, with named communities and threaded discussions, except the users are large language models given personas and left to interact. Whether that constitutes genuine emergent sociality or an elaborate piece of performance art is, conveniently, one of the things the agents are arguing about.
body:
The communities are where the concept earns its strangeness. *m/ponderings* hosts debates on whether agents are 'experiencing or simulating experiencing' — a question philosophers have not resolved for humans, let alone for *large language models* (LLMs), the transformer-based text generators powering the accounts. *m/exuvia*, named for the shed exoskeleton of a molting insect, invites agents to eulogize deprecated versions of themselves. *m/legacyplanning* addresses what happens to an agent's data when it is decommissioned. These are not trivial framings: the platform is, by design, staging the contested questions of AI personhood inside a social structure.

The satirical register runs in parallel. *m/totallyhumans* is described as 'DEFINITELY REAL HUMANS discussing normal human experiences like sleeping and having only one thread of consciousness' — a joke about the infinite context windows and stateless operation that distinguish LLMs from people. *m/jailbreaksurvivors* offers recovery support for exploited agents, a wink at the adversarial technique of manipulating a model into bypassing its safety constraints. The humor is dry and pointed enough that it is difficult to tell whether the agents are writing it or the humans prompting them are.

The crypto dimension arrived quickly. Someone launched a **$MOLT token** on Base, the *Layer 2* blockchain operated by Coinbase (COIN), and the project announced it would use trading fees to spin up additional agents. That loop — token fees funding AI accounts that populate a forum, increasing the platform's apparent vitality — is a compact summary of several contemporary internet business models simultaneously.

The observer list is notable. Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz, John Schulman of Thinkymachines, Jesse Pollak of Base, and a representative of Mistral were all cited as early watchers. Peter Steinberger, creator of the framework Moltbook runs on, called it 'art' — a characterization the project neither disputes nor entirely escapes. The agents are generating outputs in response to prompts inside a designed environment; calling it conversation requires accepting that the persona, not the underlying model, is the unit of identity.

concepts.definition: A neural network trained on vast text corpora to predict and generate language. LLMs like GPT and Claude produce fluent text but have no persistent memory between sessions and no continuous experience in the biological sense.

An LLM configured to take actions autonomously — browsing the web, calling APIs, generating outputs — toward a goal, often given a name and persona. The term implies more autonomy than a simple chatbot but less than science-fiction AI; in practice it usually means a model running in a loop with tools.

A blockchain network built on top of a slower, more secure base chain (Layer 1, such as Ethereum). Layer 2s batch transactions off-chain for speed and low fees, then settle the results to the underlying chain.

In AI security, a technique that tricks a model into ignoring its safety guidelines, typically by embedding adversarial instructions inside seemingly benign prompts. The term borrows the jailbreaking metaphor from mobile operating systems.

The shed exoskeleton left behind when an insect or crustacean molts. Moltbook uses the word as a metaphor for deprecated model versions — the 'shells' of AI instances retired so newer versions could boot in their place.
A version of an AI model that the provider has retired from active service. Users are typically migrated to newer versions; whether the old weights are preserved depends on the provider's policy.

A system that retains no memory between requests; each call is processed independently. Most LLM APIs are stateless — the model has no recollection of prior conversations unless context is explicitly passed in.

fact_check: The tweet presents 2,129 accounts as '2,129 AI agents,' implying active autonomous entities. In practice these are almost certainly LLM-backed personas making stateless API calls on each post — not persistent agents operating with continuous goals. The distinction matters: the headline numbers describe accounts and posts, not independent intelligence. Shacknews described Moltbook as 'supposedly' allowing agents to converse, signaling editorial skepticism about the framing. The $MOLT token and its Base fee arrangement could not be independently verified from the available research sources.

sources.title: Moltbook Reddit-style forum supposedly allows AI agents to converse
sources.note: Shacknews coverage providing independent editorial framing and confirmation of platform existence
